findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow.status is String; any string value is representable, so invalid state transitions (e.g. sent->draft, deleted->sent) cannot be prevented by the type system
findings.failure_mode: Caller can assign arbitrary status strings, corrupting the lease lifecycle; no invariant enforcement
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a `LeaseStatus` enum with explicit variants (e.g. `Pending`, `Validated`, `Sent`); remove `is_sent` and `sent_at_epoch_ms`

findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow.is_validated is bool; lifecycle booleans cannot enforce ordering (validated must happen before sent) and cannot represent the full state machine
findings.failure_mode: Lease can appear 'not validated' but already 'sent', or validated but never sent without explicit state tracking; booleans allow inverted/contradictory combinations
findings.fix: Encode lifecycle in the state-machine enum: `Validated` variant owns optional sent-at data; `Sent` variant owns the timestamp; transitions are explicit methods on the enum

findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow.is_sent is bool; separate from status, creating redundant and contradictory state (status could say 'draft' while is_sent is true)
findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent internal representation: status and is_sent can disagree, causing undefined workflow behavior downstream
findings.fix: Remove `is_sent` entirely; the `LeaseStatus::Sent` enum variant signals the sent state. If timestamp is needed, store it in that variant

findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow.sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64> as a bare field outside any state machine; exists independently of lifecycle booleans, allowing sent_at to be Some without is_sent=true or status='sent'
findings.failure_mode: Timestamp exists without the lease being in a sent state, or sent_at is None while is_sent is true — both are illegal states that the type system permits
findings.fix: Move timestamp into the enum variant that owns it: e.g. `Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 }` — the type system makes it impossible to have a timestamp without being in the sent state

findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow.id is String; any string is accepted as a lease ID with no validation, uniqueness guarantee, or domain semantics
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, whitespace, or malformed IDs are accepted as valid lease identifiers; collisions and parsing errors propagate into core logic
findings.fix: Introduce a `LeaseId` newtype with a smart constructor that validates the string (non-empty, format-checked) and returns a typed error

findings.problem: mark_sent unconditionally overwrites status to 'sent' and sets is_sent=true regardless of the current state; no pre-condition check, no state machine transition guard
findings.failure_mode: Any lease, regardless of lifecycle position (draft, deleted, already sent), can be forcibly set to sent — bypassing validation and causing data corruption
findings.fix: Replace with a method on the typed state-machine enum: `fn transition_to_sent(self) -> Result<Self, LeaseTransitionError>` that only succeeds from the validated state

findings.problem: mark_sent uses `item.status = "sent".to_string()` to set status by string literal, which is fallible at runtime but has no error handling — any consumer ignoring the string content creates a logic error
findings.failure_mode: If status is later changed to something requiring validation, this call silently accepts any string; no compile-time guarantee that 'sent' is a valid status value
findings.fix: Use the enum directly: `item = LeaseWorkflow { status: LeaseStatus::Sent, ..item }` via a smart constructor or builder

findings.problem: All fields of LeaseWorkflow are pub; callers can mutate any field directly, completely bypassing any invariants the struct was meant to enforce
findings.failure_mode: External code can set status="", is_validated=true, is_sent=false simultaneously — the struct represents an impossible state without any defensive boundary
findings.fix: Make all fields private; provide public methods or smart constructors that maintain invariants; use `impl` blocks for state transitions

findings.problem: No benchmark file exists for mark_sent or LeaseWorkflow; no workload, baseline, or performance claim evidence
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify that state-machine refactoring or any future changes degrade performance; no baseline for regression detection
findings.fix: Add a benchmark in benches/ that measures mark_sent / transition_to_sent throughput with realistic lease payloads

findings.problem: No cargo fmt, clippy, or test evidence produced for this crate; review cannot confirm compilation or lint compliance
findings.failure_mode: The crate may not compile under strict lint gates (clippy::arithmetic_side_effects, clippy::as_conversions, etc.)
findings.fix: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` with strict flags, and `cargo test` to produce evidence
